Shared Ontario terms and accessibility evidence were applied to six direct-HLS records. Caption availability is now recorded as available in English, sign-language as source-dependent, and audio description remains unknown; full live-stream reuse still needs written clarification.

Focused health report covered the 26 entries without retained validation history. Validation history now covers all 86 catalogue records; four official pages returned errors from this environment and Jalisco returned an HLS sample-variant warning, which remain visible as review evidence.

Official evidence updated Scottish Parliament TV, Senedd TV, Northern Ireland Assembly TV, and BC Legislature accessibility notes. Captions remain unchanged in aggregate, sign-language unknowns fell from 77 to 71, and audio-description remains unknown for all records.

Tweede Kamer live-debate and Debat Direct evidence now supports source-dependent Dutch Sign Language coverage across the three Tweede Kamer records while preserving caption availability and unknown audio-description status.

recommended_order: Review shared official-vendor rights families first, because 22 pending records use official-vendor HLS.
Review first-party HLS records next, because they are easiest to reason about technically and most valuable for playback confidence.
Review official-page fallback records after the fallback dataset stabilizes, because many should remain link-out regardless of direct playback evidence.
For accessibility, start with sources that already claim captions or interpretation in the catalogue, then replace unknown fields only with cited official evidence.
